title: 10-Year Follow-up of Closed-Wedge DFO (Distal Femoral Osteotomy): Clinical Outcomes and 10-Year Survivorship
summary: The aim of this study is to investigate the long-term outcomes of distal femoral osteotomy (DFO). This surgical procedure corrects the alignment of the thigh bone to improve load distribution within the knee joint. Patients who underwent a closed-wedge DFO approximately ten years ago will be evaluated. The study will assess long-term knee function and symptoms, with particular focus on how many patients subsequently required total knee replacement.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all patients who underwent closed-wedge distal femoral osteotomy (DFO)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Closed-wedge DFO performed at the study center
• Surgery performed on average 10 years (± 1 year) before data collection, with a targeted mean follow-up period of approximately 10 years
• Tolerance range to account for variability in the actual data collection timing
• Age ≥18 years at the time of surgery
• Available contact information (postal address or email/phone) on file
• Written or documented verbal consent to study participation
Exclusion criteria:
• Death prior to the data collection date
• No reachable contact data / no possibility of contact
•  Underlying comorbidity that makes completion of PROMs impossible (e.g., severe cognitive impairment or incapacity to consent) — unless a legal representative is available
• Patients who object to the use of their data (opt-out)
